n: Paul’s famous chapter on love. Even if he could speak every human and angelic language, without charity he would be just noise — like a clanging gong. The Corinthians prized tongues; Paul says love matters more.

f.g: Greek agape — selfless, Christlike love; the KJV renders it “charity.”
A noisy bronze gong or instrument — loud but empty.

n: Prophecy, deep understanding, all knowledge, and even mountain-moving faith amount to nothing without love.
Giving everything to the poor, or even dying as a martyr, gains nothing if done without love. Motive matters.

f.w: bestow all my goods to feed the poor
give my body to be burned
f.g: Some ancient manuscripts read “that I may boast.”

n: Paul describes love in action: it is patient and kind; it doesn’t envy, brag, or swell with pride. Mormon’s parallel description in the Book of Mormon closely matches these words.
Love isn’t rude or self-seeking, isn’t quickly angered, and doesn’t keep a record of wrongs or assume the worst.

f.g: Doesn’t plot harm or keep score of wrongs.

n: Love takes no pleasure in wrongdoing but rejoices whenever truth wins.
Love bears up under anything, keeps trusting, keeps hoping, and endures to the end.

f.g: Literally “covers” or protects; puts up with all.

n: Love never fails or ends. Prophecies, tongues, and present knowledge are temporary tools that will one day be outgrown.
Right now our knowledge and our prophecies are partial and incomplete.
When perfection comes — at the Lord’s coming and our full redemption — what is partial will be replaced.

f.g: Complete, mature; the state of full knowledge in God’s presence.

n: Like growing up, we will one day leave our childish understanding behind.

f.g: Laid aside the ways of a child.

n: Now we see God’s truths dimly, like a blurry reflection in an ancient bronze mirror. Then we will see face to face and know as fully as God knows us.

f.g: In a mirror, indistinctly — ancient mirrors were polished metal with poor reflections.

n: Faith, hope, and charity remain — but the greatest is charity, the pure love of Christ.
